stem.text: Scientists compared the density of goblet cells in the lungs and the density of mucus in the lungs of three groups of people:

items: people who do not smoke and do not have lung disease
people who smoke tobacco but do not have lung disease
people who smoke tobacco and have lung disease.

stem.text: The results are shown in the table.

rows: smokers who do not have lung disease

stem.text: What is indicated by these data?

items: There is a positive correlation (relationship) between density of goblet cells and density of mucus.
Lung disease results in an increase in goblet cell density.
There is an association between tobacco smoking and an increase in mucus density.
